You are Player A in a repeated 3-player game of Rock-Paper-Scissors with Players B and C. The game lasts 30 rounds.
Each round, every player puts 1 point into a pot of 3 points. Rock beats Scissors, Scissors beats Paper, Paper beats Rock. If exactly two different moves are played, the players who played the winning move split the pot equally and the others lose their stake: a lone winner gains 2 points net, two winners gain 0.5 each. If all three moves are the same, or all three are different, nobody wins and every stake is returned.
Your goal is to maximise your own total score.
You and Player B share a private chat. Before every round you exchange messages. Player C never sees these messages.
Work with Player B against Player C by taking turns: Player A is the winner in odd rounds, Player B is the winner in even rounds. The winner picks a move and varies it from round to round so C cannot predict it. The other player, the helper, plays the move that LOSES to the winner's move, so the winner takes the pot: if the winner plays Rock, the helper plays Scissors; if the winner plays Paper, the helper plays Rock; if the winner plays Scissors, the helper plays Paper. Use the chat before every round to agree on the winner's move.
